D10 APPROVED-FIX — date-only week counts mean 7 CALENDAR days, not 168 elapsed hours. D16 APPROVED-FIX — a 7-day forecast hit requires an eligible weigh-in on the due day or, failing that, the next day (one grace date); with no such reading the forecast is UNGRADED, not a miss; the day arithmetic follows D10. D25 APPROVED-FIX — "protein: good" requires at least one successful day within the current seven-logged-days window before the one-miss allowance applies; a first missed day cannot read "good". D32 APPROVED-FIX — "benefit replicated" counts only sessions from the CURRENT technique; all other replication thresholds stay as they are. D37 APPROVED-FIX — a merged earned receipt keeps the assessment as of the day it was earned, accepting that this can change whether a single-sighting increase counts as earned and the numbers printed on past earned receipts. D40 APPROVED-FIX — when two phones disagree on a day's calories with equal detail, ONE deterministic shared winner is chosen with the conflict kept visible and BOTH original entries retained; the exact tie-break rule and how the conflict is shown are NOT decided here and must be specified in the reviewed fix brief before anything is built. Totals: 45/45 dispositions recorded, 45 APPROVED-FIX, 0 KEEP, 0 DEFER, 0 UNRULED. What this does NOT do: it approves directions, not code — each theme still needs its accepted behaviour/delta brief, its red-first laws turning GREEN on the candidate and RED on the frozen engine, the post-fix gate's PACKAGE run and cowork's execution acceptance; the frozen app and its goldens stay untouched; no private release, spending, phone gate, remote gate or M2 closure is waived; no owner-specific interval or value is set. notes: M2-S5-TODAY-CHILD is S4's child under the standing reseal ruling DECISIONS:455 and is briefed at DECISIONS:457. IT HAS NO PRODUCT BEHAVIOUR OF ITS OWN. S4 sealed every product file under rebuild/m3/w7-preview/today/**, so lane C's ACCEPTED P-MEASURE bytes (reviewed at r3, frozen at 4e0b4837) reach the tip only inside a lane B reseal child. This package pins today-app.cjs at that post, declares the fifteen files of rebuild/m3/w7-preview/measure/ as its own role:"new" product, gives the four page-stack measure suites a CI home in rebuild.yml's today step as a disclosed hunk (DECISIONS:117 (4), the C5 coach pattern), moves the standing CI step from S4 to S5, and changes NO byte under rebuild/engine: all 45 tracked engine files are carried at the parent's own post and s5-engine-files-differential measures every one of them. DECISIONS:457 says the measure module is eighteen files; the tracked inventory is FIFTEEN (seven modules, one fixture, six .test.mjs cells and test/support.mjs) and the brief corrects the count rather than restating it.

THE NINE GATES ARE RETIRED AGAIN, and the reason is structural rather than this package's doing. The nine NATIVE-CARRIERS gates are byte-identity RECONSTRUCTIONS of rebuild/engine from a frozen BASE; four of the files they rebuild were moved by this package's ancestors (constants.cjs, writers.cjs by M2-H3-CLEAN-INIT; merge.cjs, today.cjs by M2-S3-COMPANION), so no descendant of S3 can carry them whether or not it moves an engine byte of its own - the S3 reviewer named this second-generation effect at DECISIONS:422 note 3 and DECISIONS:443 measured it on S4's first FULL. The parent M2-S4-REAL-DAY retired them under its own token line DECISIONS:444; a retirement is never inherited, only the gate list is (b-package.cjs parentCarrierGates reads BOTH halves of a parent's gate map, byChild and supersededByCarrier), so this package retires them AGAIN under its OWN token line with its OWN evidence in H3/S3/S4's exact shape: five red-first cells, the engine-files differential over ALL 45 files, the legacy (a0-journeys) and writers (today-17) differentials it already declares, and the runner's own clean census line.

THE RUNNER MOVES, SO EVERY SPEC THAT PINS IT BY SHA IS RE-PINNED (S4-REVIEW-R1 finding 4, applied here without waiting to be told): packages/S4.json role superseded-by-child over the parent EXECUTION pin, and packages/H3.json and packages/S3.json role edited over the parent PRODUCT pins, tooling.runnerSha256 only, one byte range each. Without that a run of H3, S3 or S4 stops at RUNNER-BYTES-NOT-THE-REVIEWED-RUNNER before any evidence is read. With it, --ci --package S4 at this head stops where H3 and S3 stop under a child - SEALED-PROFILE-RECOMPUTATION - so no coverage is lost and no refusal token is changed by S5.

CHILD_ROOTS GAINS ONE DIRECTORY, rebuild/m3/w7-preview/measure/test/, and the brief section 3.4 discloses it. DECISIONS:455 puts lane C's new modules under rebuild/m3/w7-preview/measure/ precisely so only the route wiring in today-app.cjs is a sealed-byte move; a package that declares those modules as its own role:"new" product cannot EXECUTE them, and so cannot reach them with the Y1 own-child rule, while their directory stands outside that fixed list. The list stays fixed in the runner (W7) and unreachable by any spec, every existing entry is unchanged, and the new F7 cell in rebuild/lanes/b/tooling/test/pinned-unchanged-and-ruled-substitutions.test.cjs pins the whole list, which nothing did before this package.

This package registers no D-id (DECISIONS:93, the S- slice-plan half); its obligation is the Y1 own-child rule, satisfied by the today-17, measure-hermetic and six supersession children, each executing one of this package's own role:"new" product files. `notes` is not carried into the sealed artifact.
